lessonTitle: Machine Safety and PPE: Guards, Emergency Stops and Safe Drilling

blocks.text: A student turns a steel bar on a centre lathe at 1200 rev/min and, in a hurry, leaves the chuck key in the chuck. When the machine starts the key is flung out of the chuck and across the workshop. Nobody is hurt this time, but the key leaves a dent in the wall at head height. Most workshop injuries come from a short list of simple habits like this one.

blocks.markdown: Safe work in a workshop rests on a hierarchy: remove or guard the hazard first, and use **personal protective equipment (PPE)** as the last line of defence for the hazards that remain. PPE is chosen for the task: what can hit you, what can burn you, what can be breathed in, and what can wrap round you.

rows: Swarf, thrown chips, entanglement with rotating work
Safety glasses, safety footwear, hair tied back, close-fitting sleeves; no gloves, rings, watches or ties
Abrasive particles, wheel fragments, noise, dust, sparks
Face shield over safety glasses, hearing protection, dust mask where needed, close-fitting clothing; wheel guard and tool rest set
Arc radiation, spatter, hot metal, fume
Welding helmet with correct filter lens, flame-resistant clothing, leather gauntlet gloves, safety boots, fume extraction or respirator as needed
Safety glasses, hair tied, no gloves or loose sleeves, workpiece clamped
blocks.caption: Representative PPE by task; follow the workshop's own rules.

blocks.title: Gloves and loose clothing near rotating parts
blocks.text: Gloves, cuffs, ties, long hair and jewellery can be caught by a rotating chuck, drill or workpiece and drawn in faster than anyone can react. Around rotating spindles work bare-handed with close-fitting sleeves; wear gloves only for handling hot or sharp stock when machines are stopped, and for welding.

blocks.markdown: **Machine guards** are physical barriers between a person and a hazardous moving part. Their purpose is to prevent contact with moving parts and to contain thrown chips, swarf and broken tools or wheel fragments. A guard must not be removed or bypassed while the machine can run.

items: **Fixed guard:** bolted in place over belts, pulleys and gears; needs a tool to remove.
**Interlocked guard:** a door or cover with a switch that stops the machine when opened and prevents starting until it is closed (for example a lathe chuck guard).
**Adjustable guard:** set to suit the work, such as a drill chuck guard. (A grinder tool rest is an adjustable work-rest that supports the work, not a guard.)
**Protective devices (not fixed guards):** a light curtain stops the machine when the area is entered, and a distance (safe-distance) arrangement keeps people out of reach.

blocks.markdown: An **emergency stop (e-stop)** is a red mushroom button on a yellow background, within easy reach of the operator. Pressing it stops hazardous motion as quickly as possible and it **latches**, so the machine cannot restart until the button is deliberately reset. It is a backup for emergencies, not a normal way of stopping, and does not replace guarding. The hand approaches the hazard at roughly 1.6 m/s (an assumed typical value; standards quote about 1600 to 2000 mm/s), the protective device and control system take a response time, and the machine then needs time to stop. The barrier must be at least that approach distance plus an intrusion allowance from the danger. Check ISO 13855/13857 and the machine's risk assessment for real designs.

blocks.caption: Grinding wheel surface speed (D in m, N in rev/min); minimum safety distance (K approach speed, typically 1.6 to 2.0 m/s, t_resp response time of the device, t_stop stopping time, C intrusion allowance; check ISO 13855/13857); combined sound level of several sources in dB.

blocks.title: Is the grinding wheel safe at this speed?
blocks.prompt: A bench grinder carries a wheel of diameter 200 mm turning at 3000 rev/min. The wheel is marked with a maximum rated surface speed of 35 m/s. Is it within its rating?

steps.text: Surface speed: v = pi D N / 60.
Evaluate: 628.3/20 = 31.4 m/s, which is below 35 m/s, so it is acceptable.

blocks.answer: 31.4 m/s is within the rating. Fitting a wheel on a faster machine could exceed its rating and risk bursting, which is why guards must contain fragments.

blocks.title: Guard distance and e-stop stopping time
blocks.prompt: A spindle takes 0.45 s to stop once the stop signal is given, and the interlock and control system respond in 0.05 s. Take the approach speed as K = 1.6 m/s (typical) and an intrusion allowance C = 0.12 m (assumed). How far must the nearest hazardous point be from an opening in the guard? (Check ISO 13855/13857 and the risk assessment for a real machine.)

steps.text: The hand may move toward the hazard during the response time and the stopping time, and may reach in a little before it is detected.
Substitute: 1.6 m/s x (0.05 s + 0.45 s) + 0.12 m.
Evaluate: 1.6 x 0.50 = 0.80 m, plus 0.12 m gives 0.92 m, so the guard opening must be at least 0.92 m from the hazard.

blocks.answer: A distance of 0.92 m or more is needed; a slower-stopping machine or slower device response needs a greater distance.

blocks.title: Adding noise from two machines
blocks.prompt: Two identical grinders each produce 82 dB at the operator's position. What is the combined level?

steps.text: Sound levels add in intensity, not in decibels: convert each to $10^{L/10}$.
Add the two equal intensities: twice one source.
Convert back: 10 log10 of the total.

blocks.answer: 85 dB, 3 dB above one machine, which is why hearing protection is needed in a workshop with several machines running.

blocks.markdown: **Pillar drill routine.** A pillar drill spins a cutter at several hundred to a few thousand rev/min. Routine matters because the common accidents are the workpiece being torn from the hand and spun, a loose item caught on the chuck and a chuck key thrown out.

items: Before starting: tie hair back, remove gloves and jewellery, fit safety glasses, check the chuck guard is in place and fully functional.
Clamp the workpiece in a machine vice or to the table; never hold it by hand. Fit the drill, tighten it and remove the chuck key before switching on.
Set the speed for the drill diameter and the material, lower the head to check clearance, then switch on and wait for full speed.
Feed steadily, withdraw to clear swarf, and use a brush after the machine has stopped, never your hand.
Shut-down: retract the drill, switch off, wait for the spindle to stop on its own (do not stop it by hand), remove the drill if required, clean the table and isolate the machine.

blocks.title: Order matters
blocks.text: Marks in procedure questions go for the sequence: protect yourself, secure the workpiece, remove the key, then start; stop, wait, clean, isolate. Say why each step is there.

points: PPE is chosen for the task: glasses and no gloves for turning and drilling, face shield, hearing protection and dust control for grinding, helmet, flame-resistant clothing and gauntlets for welding.
Guards prevent contact with moving parts and contain thrown fragments; an e-stop is a latching red mushroom button that stops hazardous motion but does not replace guards.
A pillar drill needs PPE, a clamped workpiece, the chuck key removed before starting, and a deliberate shut-down: stop, wait for rotation to stop, clean and isolate.

questions.stem: A student is about to turn a steel bar on a centre lathe. Which choice of dress and PPE is correct?

options.text: Safety glasses, hair tied back, close-fitting sleeves and no gloves or jewellery
Safety glasses and thin cotton gloves so that the swarf cannot cut the hands
A loose lab coat and a wristwatch so that the sleeves stay clean
No eye protection because the chuck guard stops all chips

questions.correctOptionText: Safety glasses, hair tied back, close-fitting sleeves and no gloves or jewellery

distractorRationale.b: Gloves can be caught by the rotating work and pull the hand in, so they should not be worn.
distractorRationale.c: Loose clothing and watches can be caught by rotating parts.
distractorRationale.d: Guards do not stop all chips, so eye protection is still needed.

questions.explanation: Around a rotating chuck anything loose can be wound in, so close-fitting clothing, tied hair and no gloves or jewellery are required, with safety glasses against chips. The guard does not replace eye protection.

questions.stem: An arc welder is joining steel plate. Which PPE is most appropriate?

options.text: A welding helmet with the correct filter lens, flame-resistant clothing and leather gauntlet gloves
Ordinary safety glasses and cotton overalls
A grinding face shield only
Hearing protection and a dust mask only

questions.correctOptionText: A welding helmet with the correct filter lens, flame-resistant clothing and leather gauntlet gloves

distractorRationale.b: Ordinary glasses give no protection against arc radiation, and cotton can burn or be pierced by spatter.
distractorRationale.c: A clear grinding shield does not filter the arc radiation.
distractorRationale.d: These do not protect eyes and skin from arc radiation and spatter.

questions.explanation: Arc welding gives intense ultraviolet and visible radiation, spatter and hot metal, so the eyes need a filter lens and the skin needs flame-resistant clothing and gloves. Dust masks or glasses do not provide this.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of an interlocked guard on a machine such as a lathe chuck?

options.text: It stops the machine when opened and prevents starting until it is closed
It is a normal way to stop the machine at the end of a job
It lets operators hold the workpiece by hand more easily
It reduces the machine noise to a safe level

questions.correctOptionText: It stops the machine when opened and prevents starting until it is closed

distractorRationale.b: Normal stopping uses the machine controls; the interlock is a safety device.
distractorRationale.c: Guards prevent contact and do not change how the work is held.
distractorRationale.d: Guards are not primarily noise controls.

questions.explanation: An interlock links the guard to the control circuit so that the hazard cannot be reached while the machine runs and the machine cannot start with the guard open. It protects against contact and fragments.

questions.stem: What happens when an emergency stop button is pressed on a correctly designed machine?

options.text: Hazardous motion stops and the button latches, so the machine cannot restart until it is deliberately reset
The machine pauses and restarts automatically when the button is released
The guards open so that the operator can reach the work
The power is reduced, but the spindle runs on until it is stopped by hand

questions.correctOptionText: Hazardous motion stops and the button latches, so the machine cannot restart until it is deliberately reset

distractorRationale.b: A restart without a deliberate reset is dangerous; the button latches.
distractorRationale.c: Guards stay closed to keep people away from the moving parts.
distractorRationale.d: An e-stop stops motion; stopping by hand is not part of the design.

questions.explanation: The e-stop stops hazardous motion and latches, preventing an unexpected restart. A deliberate reset after the cause is cleared is required.

questions.stem: Before switching on a pillar drill, which check is essential?

options.text: The workpiece is clamped, the chuck key has been removed and the chuck guard is in place
The workpiece is held firmly in a gloved hand
The drill speed has been set to the maximum
The swarf has been cleared from the table by hand while the spindle idles

questions.correctOptionText: The workpiece is clamped, the chuck key has been removed and the chuck guard is in place

distractorRationale.b: Holding by hand lets the drill tear the work out of the hand; gloves can also be caught.
distractorRationale.c: Maximum speed is not always right and the check is about securing the work.
distractorRationale.d: Swarf is cleared with a brush after the machine has stopped.

questions.explanation: Clamping prevents the workpiece spinning, and a chuck key left in the chuck is thrown out when the spindle starts. These checks are done before power is applied.

questions.stem: A grinding wheel of diameter 150 mm runs at 4500 rev/min. What is its surface speed in m/s? (Its rated maximum is 33 m/s.)
questions.explanation: The speed is $\pi\times0.15\times4500/60=35.3$ m/s. This exceeds the wheel's rating of 33 m/s, so it is unsafe to run this wheel at that speed.

questions.stem: A saw spindle needs 0.55 s to stop after the stop signal, and the interlock responds in 0.05 s. Assuming an approach speed of 1.6 m/s and an intrusion allowance of 0.12 m, what is the minimum distance in metres between the guard opening and the hazardous point, using $S=K(t_{resp}+t_{stop})+C$?
questions.explanation: The minimum distance is $S=1.6\times(0.05+0.55)+0.12=0.96+0.12=1.08$ m. A machine that stops more slowly, or a device that responds more slowly, requires a greater distance from the opening to the hazard.

questions.stem: A workshop has two machines producing 91 dB and 88 dB at the same bench. What is the combined sound level in dB?
questions.explanation: Convert to intensities: $10^{9.1}+10^{8.8}=1.259\times10^{9}+6.31\times10^{8}=1.89\times10^{9}$. Taking $10\log_{10}$ gives 92.8 dB. The result is only slightly above the louder machine, because decibels add on a logarithmic scale.

questions.stem: Describe a safe start-up and shut-down routine for a pillar drill, explaining the reason for each step.
markingGuide: Before start: PPE (safety glasses), hair tied back, no gloves, loose clothing or jewellery
Check guard in place, workpiece clamped in a vice or to the table
Chuck key removed before switching on (it would be thrown out)
Set a suitable speed, check clearance, switch on and let it reach speed
Shut down: retract, switch off, wait until the spindle stops without touching it, clear swarf with a brush, isolate
questions.explanation: The routine prevents entanglement, ejection of parts and contact with a moving tool. A good answer gives the sequence and the reason for each step.

questions.stem: A technician is regrinding a tool on a bench grinder. Name the PPE and guarding required and explain why gloves are not worn around rotating spindles but are worn for welding.
markingGuide: Eye and face protection (face shield over safety glasses) against particles and fragments
Hearing protection and dust control or mask
Wheel guard fitted and tool rest set close to the wheel
Gloves can be caught by rotating parts and pull the hand in
Welding gloves protect against heat and spatter and no rotating parts are present
questions.explanation: PPE is selected for the hazard: particles, noise and dust for grinding, heat for welding. Gloves are hazardous where rotating parts can catch them and useful where heat is the hazard.
